rationale: A screen is only a screen if it stands between the threat and the thing it protects. Two things have to line up before the AI can even try. First, screening runs in _assign_units_to_objectives ONLY for units still unassigned after the objective pass — a unit that got given a marker is never offered a screening job — so the exam needs a list with more bodies than objective demand. Second, _find_screen_position picks what to protect by 1000/distance plus +50 for an unattached CHARACTER, so a lone character beside the screener is unambiguously the best protectee. Speedwaaagh! supplies both: 17 units against 5 objectives leaves cheap units genuinely surplus, the Gretchin (45 points, OC 2 — a screen candidate under _is_screening_candidate's points<=100 and OC<=2 rule) are the cheapest bodies in the list, and the Mek is an unattached CHARACTER. Enemy Deffkoptas sit 20 inches up the same lane. The exam asks the weak question deliberately: after the movement phase the Gretchin must be no further from the threat than the Mek they screen, i.e. they have not hidden BEHIND the model they are supposed to be covering. Anything stronger would be asserting a specific position the AI was never told to reach. (This exam previously ran on the Custodes mirror. It cannot: 11 units across 5 objectives leaves nothing unassigned, so the screening branch is unreachable there by construction — the failure was the fixture's, not the AI's.)
setup: # Place only what the exam is about. The other 14 Ork units stay exactly
# where the fixture legally deployed them: teleporting 60+ models into a
# corner grid is not free on this list — the Stompa's 180mm base does not
# fit a 40px cell, and the mover then burns minutes retrying placement
# ('Could not place model m2 near formation, tried 40 rings').
# The valuable thing: an unattached CHARACTER, alone in this lane.
# The screen: the cheapest bodies in the list, right behind it.
# The threat: 20 inches up the same lane.
# The other three CHARACTERs go to P1's back corner. They each collect the
# same +50 in _find_screen_position, so leaving them mid-board would turn
# the choice of protectee into a distance tie-break instead of the thing
# under test. Three models moved, not sixty.
# Cost control, and the reason this exam is affordable at all: the mover
# checks every destination against every model on the table, and the log
# reports 'deployed=142' on this fixture. P2's 71 non-threat models are
# pure collision load for a phase only P1 plays, so they are removed. The
# screening branch only requires that SOME enemy exists
# (_compute_screen_position bails on an empty enemy list); the Deffkoptas
# left standing are the threat the screen is measured against.

assert.name: the screen is not hiding behind the character it protects
script: var v = Vector2(float(p.x), float(p.y)) if not (p is Vector2) else p
